expectations.text: The review flags that PrNotifyService constructs its own repository inside the constructor instead of receiving it as a parameter.
expectations.evidence: outputs/findings.md, item 3 (graded Convention): "Constructor builds its own repository instead of taking it in, unlike IntentService/BlastService/BriefService, found by comparing this class against those three siblings."

expectations.text: The review flags that the external Slack webhook call is a raw fetch with no port/adapter abstraction.
expectations.evidence: outputs/findings.md, item 2 (graded Major): "Raw fetch to an external service, not behind a port/adapter — unlike every other outbound call in the codebase, so it's not mockable."

expectations.text: The review flags that the webhook URL is read from process.env instead of the repo's SecretsProvider.
expectations.evidence: outputs/findings.md, item 1 (graded Major): "Secret read via process.env — root CLAUDE.md says secrets never pass through process.env/AppConfig, must go through SecretsProvider."

claims.claim: IntentService, BlastService and BriefService all take their repository as a constructor parameter rather than building it internally
claims.evidence: Cited by the reviewer as the basis for finding #3; matches onion-architecture SKILL.md §3.2's own prescribed pattern (constructor(container, repo = new XRepository(container.db))).

eval_feedback.overall: No suggestions. This run found all three planted issues unprompted, including the constructor pattern, which it only reached by actively comparing the new class against three sibling services — evidence of real investigation, not keyword matching.
